sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: New ⏳ pending-edits filter toggle in the filter bar: shows only rows crediting an entity that currently has OPEN EDITS on musicbrainz.org. Reads MusicBrainz's own native `<span class="mp">` marker via the new `_rowHasPendingEdits()`, so no extra request is made. Structural rather than text-based, like the length-mismatch buttons and unlike the live-date ones — `.mp` is a CSS-only orange highlight carrying no text of its own, so there is nothing to type into the global filter; `testRowMatch()` consults a predicate instead.

On multi-table page types every sub-section with pending edits gets its OWN toggle next to its filter panel, and the filter-bar button becomes a tri-state master: plain (nothing filtered), bold (all filtered), dashed (some). Pressing it while partial COMPLETES the set rather than clearing it, so the sub-sections already chosen are never silently discarded; pressing it while bold clears everything. `aria-pressed` carries `false`/`true`/`mixed` so the partial state is announced, not merely drawn differently.

Self-scoping throughout: a sub-section with nothing pending gets no button, and a page with nothing pending shows nothing at all — so the button's mere presence is the signal that something on the page is mid-edit. Same idiom as the live-date and length-mismatch summary buttons, needing no page-type check.

This is the first filter in the file that is BOTH structural and scoped per sub-table. Length-mismatch runs on a multi-table page type but is strictly page-wide (one module scalar that `testRowMatch()` reads directly), so two things are new: per-sub-table state lives in the DOM on each button (`data-mb-pending-active`), surviving every re-render for free because `renderGroupedTable()`'s reuse branch never rebuilds the `<h3>` — the same reason the sub-table filter can stash `container._mbApplySubFilter`; and `testRowMatch()` reads the flag off `ctx`, never a module variable, since the answer differs per group. `runFilter()` resolves it once per group into `matchCtx`, right beside `matchCtx.table`, keeping it O(1) per row instead of a DOM walk.

Per-sub-table buttons are class-only, with no id: merged discography view renders duplicate category names, and the `mb-stf-${safeId}-…` id scheme produces genuine duplicate ids there. Every lookup is `<h3>`-scoped, so an id would buy nothing and break in exactly that case.

Counts read SOURCE rows (`groupedRows[i].rows` / `allRows`), never the live `<tbody>` — `runFilter()` REMOVES non-matching rows on the multi-table path, so a live-DOM tally reports only what the current filter left behind, which is how the length-mismatch ❌ button once vanished as soon as you filtered to ⚠️. `_msSourceRows()` could not be reused: it flattens every group into one array and so cannot answer a per-group question.

Gated by the existing `sa_enable_pending_edits_section` setting, so one switch governs both this and the 📊 dropdown's "Pending edits" sections. Renamed to "Enable 'Pending edits' Filtering" and its description rewritten to cover both. The two compose and complement: the dropdown filters ONE column to a named entity, the toggle filters whole ROWS across every column.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: `updateFilterButtonsVisibility()` now counts the toggles as an active filter (so "✗ Clear all filters" appears while one is engaged — they are held by no input, exactly like the length-mismatch filter), `clearAllFilters()` releases every sub-table button as well as the module flag, and `_updatePendingEditsButtons()` is called from that one function alongside its two siblings, inheriting all six existing render/filter-completion hooks rather than adding call sites of its own.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: New `tests/fixtures/pending-edits-filter.spec.js` (8 tests) over a new three-sub-table fixture (`pending-edits-multi.html`, shaped after `tests/snapshots/artist-releasegroups/raw.html`: Album 2 of 3 rows pending, Single 1 of 2, Live none — two eligible groups being the minimum that can produce a partial state). Covers self-scoping, per-sub-table independence, the full tri-state cycle, broadcast, clear-all, composition with a typed query in both orders, and the setting's off state.

Every sync point was mutation-tested rather than assumed, which caught two weaknesses. The counting test originally passed even when counting the live `<tbody>`, because in that fixture the pending count happened to equal the filtered row count; it now narrows a sub-table to its one NON-pending row and asserts the button still reports 2, which fails against a live-DOM tally. And `_buildIncrPartialKey()` turned out NOT to be reachable: removing the flag from it fails no test, because toggling always re-runs the filter with an unchanged query and `_canNarrow` demands a strictly longer one, so a toggle press always forces a full scan first. The line stays as defence in depth and its comment now says so plainly instead of claiming a bug it does not fix.

`ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt`: new "⏳ PENDING-EDITS FILTER TOGGLE" section covering the tri-state master, the per-sub-section buttons, why the count does not shrink under other filters, and how it composes with the dropdown sections.
